findings.description: Indexes strcomp[i] while iterating i up to word.length() without verifying strcomp has the same length.
Calls ladder.back() without ensuring ladder is non-empty.
Doesn't verify that the dictionary file was successfully opened.
Uses the anti-pattern while(!inFile.eof()) to read.
Doesn't validate std::cin >> word >> target succeeded.
No validation that start and target have the same non-zero length before processing.
Recursive DFS can blow the stack on large dictionaries or deep search paths.
With no visited set, it can revisit states, exacerbating resource consumption.
